{{short description|Expansion of exponentials of trigonometric functions in the basis of their harmonics}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Jacobi–Anger expansion''' (or '''Jacobi–Anger identity''') is an expansion of exponentials of [[trigonometric function]]s in the basis of their harmonics. It is useful in physics (for example, to [[plane wave expansion|convert]] between [[plane wave]]s and [[cylindrical wave]]s), and in [[signal processing]] (to describe [[frequency modulation|FM]] signals). This identity is named after the 19th-century mathematicians [[Carl Gustav Jacob Jacobi|Carl Jacobi]] and [[Carl Theodor Anger]].

The most general identity is given by:<ref name=Colton_Kress_32>Colton & Kress (1998) p. 32.</ref><ref name=Cuyt_et_al_344>Cuyt ''et al.'' (2008) p. 344.</ref>

:<math>
  e^{i z \cos \theta} \equiv \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty} i^n\, J_n(z)\, e^{i n \theta},
</math>

where <math>J_n(z)</math> is the <math>n</math>-th [[Bessel function of the first kind]] and <math>i</math> is the [[imaginary unit]], <math display="inline">i^2=-1.</math> 
Substituting <math display="inline">\theta</math> by <math display="inline">\theta-\frac{\pi}{2}</math>, we also get:

:<math>
  e^{i z \sin \theta} \equiv \sum_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}       J_n(z)\, e^{i n \theta}.
</math>

Using the relation <math>J_{-n}(z) = (-1)^n\, J_{n}(z),</math> valid for integer <math>n</math>, the expansion becomes:<ref name=Colton_Kress_32/><ref name=Cuyt_et_al_344/>

:<math>e^{i z \cos \theta} \equiv J_0(z)\, +\, 2\, \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\, i^n\, J_n(z)\, \cos\, (n \theta).</math>

==Real-valued expressions==
The following real-valued variations are often useful as well:<ref>Abramowitz & Stegun (1965) [http://www.math.sfu.ca/~cbm/aands/page_361.htm p. 361, 9.1.42–45]</ref>

:<math>
\begin{align}
  \cos(z \cos \theta) &\equiv J_0(z)+2 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^n J_{2n}(z) \cos(2n \theta),
  \\
  \sin(z \cos \theta) &\equiv -2 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty}(-1)^n J_{2n-1}(z) \cos\left[\left(2n-1\right) \theta\right],
  \\
  \cos(z \sin \theta) &\equiv J_0(z)+2 \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} J_{2n}(z) \cos(2n \theta),
  \\
  \sin(z \sin \theta) &\equiv 2 \sum_{ n=1 }^{\infty} J_{2n-1}(z) \sin\left[\left(2n-1\right) \theta\right].
\end{align}
</math>
